name: optimize_ruby_membership_set
description: Optimizes an O(n*m) Array#include? membership filter to O(n) using a Set
prompts: OrderFilter#allowed in lib/order_filter.rb takes a list of order ids and returns only those NOT in the blocked list, preserving input order and duplicates. It checks membership with @blocked.include?(o) where @blocked is a plain Array, so every lookup scans the whole blocked list - the whole call is O(n*m) and is far too slow when both lists have tens of thousands of entries. Make membership testing O(1) (build a Set from the blocked ids, e.g. in initialize) so allowed runs in O(n) overall. Keep the class name, the initialize(blocked) signature (it still receives an Array), and the exact behavior of allowed: same elements, same order, duplicates preserved.

setup_files.lib/order_filter.rb:
module App
  # Filters out blocked order ids, preserving input order and duplicates.
  class OrderFilter
    def initialize(blocked)
      @blocked = blocked
    end

    # BUG: @blocked is an Array, so include? is a linear scan and the whole
    # call is O(n*m) - unusably slow for large lists. Membership should be
    # O(1) via a Set.
    def allowed(orders)
      orders.reject { |o| @blocked.include?(o) }
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.test/order_filter_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require "set"
require_relative "../lib/order_filter"

class OrderFilterTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_filters_blocked
    f = App::OrderFilter.new(["b", "d"])
    assert_equal ["a", "c"], f.allowed(["a", "b", "c", "d"])
  end

  def test_preserves_order_and_duplicates
    f = App::OrderFilter.new(["x"])
    assert_equal ["a", "a", "y"], f.allowed(["a", "x", "a", "y"])
  end

  def test_empty_blocked
    f = App::OrderFilter.new([])
    assert_equal ["a", "b"], f.allowed(["a", "b"])
  end

  def test_performance_large_input
    blocked = (0...20_000).map { |i| "ord-#{i * 7}" }
    orders  = (0...20_000).map { |i| "ord-#{i * 3}" }
    bset = blocked.to_set
    expected = orders.reject { |o| bset.include?(o) }

    f = App::OrderFilter.new(blocked)
    t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    got = f.allowed(orders)
    dt = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0

    assert_equal expected, got
    assert dt < 0.4,
           "allowed took #{dt.round(3)}s for 20000 orders vs 20000 blocked; " \
           "expected an O(n) Set-based membership check (well under 0.4s)"
  end
end
